pr.title: Have find exit as grep does, and correct a refused-address row
pr.head: 022917bb9ee434933a47e35503e3c5a423aa6474

summary: multipass is a command-line password manager. Its websites plan, which is ready but not built yet, adds a website field to each entry and a multipass find <url> command that prints the names of the entries for a web page, so a browser extension or the Mac app can offer the right login on the right site.

A script that calls find needs to know whether the page simply has no entry or whether something went wrong, such as a wrong passphrase. Most multipass commands exit with status 1 on every error today, so if find also exited 1 for "no match", the script would have to read the error text to tell the two apart. The plan left that choice to the owner.

This pull request records the owner's answer: find exits as grep does. Every other command keeps the statuses it has today: 1 on any error, except upgrade, which passes the installer's status through and stops with 65 or 69 when its own checks fail. The pull request changes only the plan document.

StatusMeaning
0At least one entry matches.
1No entry matches. Related entries, if any, are named on stderr.
2Any error, such as a usage error, a refused page address, a wrong passphrase, a store that cannot be read, or a declined Touch ID sheet.
While moving the acceptance rows for refused addresses to status 2, the author also fixed one row that contradicted the plan's own parsing rules, as the group below explains.

cards.title: Where the review stands
cards.html:
• The first review's finding is fixed: the plan now states upgrade's statuses correctly, in § 2.2 and § 6 alike.
  • All four suggestions from the first review are taken. Status 2 covers every error, the changes-by-file rows for src/main.rs and README.md name the statuses, § 4 has a wrong-passphrase row, and the look-alike address test covers the corrected case.
  • One new suggestion: say that find's usage errors exit 2 and add a row for them, because upgrade's own usage errors still exit 1.
  • One follow-up is still owed: the plan does not say how find opens the store while a Touch ID session is unlocked.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Exit status: the number a command returns to the shell, which a script tests with if or $?.
  • Usage error: a command typed wrongly, such as multipass find with no address.
  • Authority: the part of a web address between :// and the first /, ?, or #; it holds the host and port.
  • Refused address: a page address the plan's strict parser rejects because a browser would read its host differently.
  • Session unlock: the background agent that keeps the store open between commands and asks for a touch of Touch ID instead of the passphrase.

groups.title: The websites plan
groups.kicker: How find reports its result, and one corrected acceptance row
intro: Four parts of the plan change. § 2.2, which describes matching, gains the table of exit statuses and says what every other command keeps. § 2.5, the changes by file, says that src/main.rs returns find's status itself and that the README gives the statuses. § 4, the acceptance criteria, moves its rows for refused addresses from "fails" to "exits 2" and adds rows for a match and a wrong passphrase. § 6, the plan's decided questions, records the choice and the alternative the owner rejected: status 1 for every failure.

The corrected row concerns the address https://evil.example\@github.com/. The plan refuses an address that holds an @ in its authority, because a browser reads the text before the @ as a user name and password. It runs that check before every other rule and never repeats such an address in an error, since the text before the @ may be a real password. The old row expected an error naming the address because of its backslash, which broke that rule. The row now expects the @ error without the address, and a new row covers a backslash on its own, which may be named.

files.note: The plan for the website field and find: § 2.2 gains the exit-status table, § 2.5 and § 4 follow it, and § 6 records the decision.

checks.text: § 2.2: checked against src/main.rs and src/upgrade.rs. main returns run_upgrade directly, which exits with the installer's status or with 65 or 69, and every other command's error becomes ExitCode::FAILURE, status 1.

§ 2.2: upgrade's route does not cover usage errors. parse returns them to main first, so multipass upgrade 0.2 exits 1. To make find's usage errors exit 2, as the table says, the implementation has to handle them in parse's path too.
§ 2.2: the quoted Touch ID error matches NOT_APPROVED in src/main.rs.

§ 4: checked against § 2.1. The authority of https://evil.example\@github.com/ runs to the first /, so it holds the @, the @ check runs first, and its error must not name the address. The new row on line 151 holds no @, so naming it is allowed.
